module: GCA AI Quant Access service delivery
scope: The GCA Service Delivery Playbook defines an operator-reviewed workflow for account intake, read-only GCA wallet verification, service request queueing and pre-review cancellation, manual report delivery, and credit usage records. It is not automated trading, not live production exchange routing, not custody, not financial advice, and not a promise of any market outcome.

deliveryFlow.description: User registers through the official account path and submits one Base wallet for read-only GCA balance review.
Wallet eligibility is checked with ERC-20 balanceOf data; no signature, transaction, private key, or seed phrase is required.

An authenticated account can submit one catalog service, a non-sensitive scope, and a client request ID through the controlled account UI. The Worker applies the server catalog unit and queues the request for operator review.

Before any operator review, the matching account can permanently cancel its own queued request. Retries are idempotent; cancellation does not refund or restore credits, write a wallet, transfer tokens, create trading permission, or delete audit history.
Operator records an append-only approved, needs-more-information, or rejected decision after reviewing scope and safety boundaries.
Only an approved request can be marked delivered. The operator confirms completion and supplies a non-sensitive delivery reference; no wallet action or trading permission is created.
The delivered review uses the server catalog unit and commits one linked credit usage record, ledger deduction, append-only review, and delivered status in one D1 batch. Replays cannot deduct twice.

After completed delivery, the matching account can acknowledge receipt once. The deterministic receipt is idempotent and does not refund or deduct credits, write a wallet, transfer tokens, or create trading permission.

releaseBoundaries: The playbook is public and local operator recording is ready.
Production service-request, service-review, and credit-usage Worker routes are live and token-protected after all release gates passed.
Authenticated accounts can submit device-key protected service requests and read a redacted account-scoped history.
Service requests do not deduct credits by themselves.
Manual decisions are append-only, delivery requires prior approval, and the account history returns a redacted latest review.
Credit usage is recorded only with completed delivery and at most once for each service request.
The matching device-key account can acknowledge completed delivery once without changing credits, wallet state, tokens, or trading permission.
Member status does not create automatic transfers or trading permission.
The workflow does not collect private keys, seed phrases, wallet signatures, custody permissions, withdrawal permissions, or exchange API secrets.

safeClaims: GCA has published an operator-reviewed service delivery playbook for GCA AI Quant Access workflows.
The workflow covers account intake, read-only wallet verification, service request queueing, manual report delivery, and credit usage records.
The controlled account UI can create a device-key protected request and read its redacted account-scoped history.
Production service-request, service-review, and credit-usage Worker routes are live, token-protected, and verified by public and admin read-only smoke checks.
The server catalog determines the service credit unit; submission neither reserves nor deducts credits.
The operator review route stores append-only decisions, requires approval before delivery, and settles the catalog credit unit at most once.
The user history shows the latest redacted decision and settlement without returning operator notes or reviewer identity.
After completed delivery, the matching device-key account can write one idempotent receipt marker without any credit or wallet effect.
Before any manual review, the matching device-key account can permanently cancel its queued request; retries are idempotent and have no credit or wallet effect.
The workflow is no-custody, does not request wallet signatures, and does not create automatic trading access.
doNotClaim: service delivery is automatic or does not require manual approval
credits are automatically deducted before operator review
the same service request can deduct credits more than once
a delivery receipt is a refund, a second deduction, wallet settlement, token transfer, or dispute decision
a queued-request cancellation is a refund, credit restoration, wallet settlement, token transfer, audit-history deletion, or cancellation after review has started
GCA AI Quant Access executes trades for users
reports are financial advice or trading signals
